Reproducing Petersen & Buzsaki (2020) from dandiset 000059¶

Paper. Petersen PC, Buzsaki G (2020). Cooling of medial septum reveals theta phase lag coordination of hippocampal cell assemblies. Neuron 107, 731-744. doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2020.05.023. This attempt used the full text of the accepted author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC7442698). The supplementary PDF could not be obtained, so supplementary figures are tested only where the main text states their result.

Dandiset. DANDI:000059, version 0.250624.0444. The paper cites no DANDI version (its data statement points to the lab's website and CRCNS). This is the most recent published version. Version 0.230907.2101 holds the same 100 files with the same blobs. The first version, 0.210812.1514, held 54 combined files, among them four sessions without behaviour, and its files have no trials table, which every behavioural claim here needs; the data check shows this.

Code. The paper's MATLAB code is public (GitHub petersenpeter/Code_Petersen_Buzsaki_Neuron_2020, commit aec2f7e, read for this attempt, not run). It fixes the theta measures, the per-trial averages, the onset-aligned trial series behind Figures 2G, 2H and 6, and the lists of sessions; cooling.py says which parameter comes from where.

What the dandiset holds. 50 behavioural sessions of five rats on the figure-8 maze, each with a processed file (trials with cooling state and choice error, position, speed, MS temperature, and units in 24 sessions) and a raw file (20 kHz wide-band and 1250 Hz LFP). The files carry no cell types and no place field definitions, and no hippocampal temperature recordings.

The notebook streams every file at the pinned version. One bootstrap draws random numbers; it has its own seeded generator.

started = time.time()
S = C.sessions()
with ProcessPoolExecutor(6) as ex:
    beh = dict(zip(S.index, ex.map(C.behaviour_session, S.index)))
unit_keys = [k for k, r in beh.items() if S.loc[k, "in_code_list"] and r["has_state"] and r["n_good_units"] > 0]
with ProcessPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
    units = dict(zip(unit_keys, ex.map(C.unit_session, unit_keys)))

from dandi.dandiapi import DandiAPIClient
with DandiAPIClient() as client:
    vers = {}
    for v in ["0.210812.1514", "0.230907.2101", "0.250624.0444"]:
        assets = list(client.get_dandiset(C.DANDISET_ID, v).get_assets())
        vers[v] = {a.path: (a.size, getattr(a, "blob", None)) for a in assets}
    old_asset = next(a for a in client.get_dandiset(C.DANDISET_ID, "0.210812.1514").get_assets()
                     if "MS10-170319" in a.path)
    old_url = old_asset.get_content_url(follow_redirects=1, strip_query=True)
for v, a in vers.items():
    print(f"{v}: {len(a)} files, {sum(s for s, _ in a.values()) / 1e12:.2f} TB")
same = vers["0.230907.2101"].keys() == vers["0.250624.0444"].keys() and all(
    vers["0.230907.2101"][p] == vers["0.250624.0444"][p] for p in vers["0.250624.0444"])
print("0.230907.2101 and 0.250624.0444 hold the same paths, sizes and blobs:", same)
old_sessions = sorted({C.session_key(p) for p in vers["0.210812.1514"]})
new_sessions = sorted({C.session_key(p) for p in vers["0.250624.0444"]})
print("sessions only in 0.210812.1514:", sorted(set(old_sessions) - set(new_sessions)))
f_old = C.open_h5(old_url)
print("0.210812.1514, file", old_asset.path.split("/")[-1], "has a trials table:", "intervals/trials" in f_old,
      "; has units:", "units" in f_old, "; has LFP:", "processing/ecephys/LFP" in f_old)
f_old.close()

The dandiset holds 50 sessions; the paper reports 53 in five rats, and the code's behavioural list has 53. 47 of the code's sessions are here; six are not (MS12-170712, -170715, MS13-171204, -171205, -171206, MS21-180806). Three sessions here are not in that list: MS10-170307, and the two sessions of 2018-07-19, which the code's recording list describes as controls without cooling. MS21-180627 has a trials table without the cooling state, and MS21-180712 has no trials. Units are curated (good, good2, mua, noise) in 17 sessions; in seven (the six MS10 sessions with units and MS12-170723) every unit is 'unsorted', so no unit can be selected there. No file has a cell type, a place field, or an electrode location (every location is 'unknown'). The subject age is a range (P3M/P6M).

Position is stored in centimetres (conversion 0.01 to metres) and speed in cm/s. The maze circle fitted to the arm positions has a radius of about 50 cm (diameter about 100 cm against the 110 cm of the Methods, which may be the outer edge of the track). Position is sampled at 120 Hz in the 2017-2018 MS12 to MS22 sessions and at 40 Hz in the MS10 sessions.

The code's recording list gives no temperature channel for the nine MS10 sessions and for the two 2018-07-19 control sessions (ch_temp = 0). In the dandiset these eleven sessions still have a temperature trace, and it is not a recording. MS10-170307 is a constant 37.0 C. Each of the other ten runs from 17.0 to 37.0 C (exactly in nine; MS10-170313 reaches 16.98 C) and sits at exactly 37.0 C for 16% to 35% of its samples (frac_at_max), while no recorded trace takes its maximum value more than once (frac_at_max 0). These are smooth curves of a cooling time course, consistent with a model; their roughness (SD of the second difference) does not tell them apart from recordings. The trials of the two control sessions are also labelled with cooling states. Recorded traces contain artefacts up to 50 C in some sessions (T_max above).

def state_theta(tr):
    m = tr.groupby("state").theta_freq.mean()
    return {s: round(m.get(s, np.nan), 3) for s in ["Pre-Cooling", "Cooling on", "Cooling off", "Post-Cooling"]}

    th = state_theta(tr)
    pre = tr.theta_freq[tr.state == "Pre-Cooling"]; cool = tr.theta_freq[tr.state == "Cooling on"]
    print(f"  {k}: {th}; cooling minus pre {cool.mean() - pre.mean():+.3f} Hz, rank-sum P = {stats.ranksums(cool, pre).pvalue:.2g}")

Over the code's sessions the theta slowing is strongest with no shift, and in each session the best shift is within 120 s of zero (29 at zero); the cooling lasts about ten minutes, so the contrast changes slowly with the shift. The LFP and the trial table share a clock as far as this check can tell. In the eight MS10 sessions theta slows by 0.37 to 1.08 Hz in the "Cooling on" trials, so they were cooled, as the code's hand-noted onsets say, although their temperature is not a recording. In the two control sessions the "Cooling on" trials differ from the pre trials by -0.20 and +0.44 Hz, the weakest contrasts but one (MS12-170723, +0.50 Hz, has a recorded temperature drop) against a median of -0.82 Hz in the other sessions. This is consistent with the code's description of them as sessions without cooling; it does not prove it.

In eleven of the thirteen unit sessions the spatial information of the maps falls 40-fold or more when the spikes are shifted by 60 s, so spikes and position share a clock as far as this check can tell. In MS21-180621 and MS22-180621 it does not fall (0.23 against 0.28, and 0.12 against 0.11 bits/spike), and these sessions have 4 and 0 place cells. Their spikes are locked to theta (mean resultant length 0.37 and 0.34, against 0.11 when shifted), so they belong to the recording; the outputs cannot say whether the spike and position clocks differ there or the units were not spatially tuned (both are the rat's first session). The clock of spikes and position could not be established in these two sessions, and they are left out of the unit claims. Theta phase locking falls with a 0.5 s shift in every session, so spikes and LFP share a clock. Spikes and the wide-band data share it too, since mean waveforms at the spike times have the shape of action potentials (below).

Session sets used below (fixed in the claims file): BEH, the 45 sessions of the code's behavioural list that are here and have cooling states; TEMP, the 37 BEH sessions with a recorded temperature (BEH without MS10); UNIT, the 11 BEH sessions with curated units whose spikes carry spatial information (the 13 with curated units less the two 180621 sessions); FIG5, the 9 UNIT sessions of the code's Figure 5 list.

Helpers for the claims¶

Wilcoxon signed-rank and rank-sum tests are two-sided (scipy, exact where scipy uses it). Each test prints its n.

In [16]:
def wsr(a, b=None):
    a = np.asarray(a, float)
    d = a if b is None else a - np.asarray(b, float)
    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]
    if len(d) < 2 or np.all(d == 0):
        return np.nan, len(d)
    return float(stats.wilcoxon(d).pvalue), len(d)

def rks(a, b):
    a, b = np.asarray(a, float), np.asarray(b, float)
    a, b = a[np.isfinite(a)], b[np.isfinite(b)]
    return float(stats.ranksums(a, b).pvalue), len(a), len(b)

def within(x, value, tol):
    return bool(np.isfinite(x) and abs(x - value) <= tol + 1e-12)

def subj(k):
    return k.split("-")[0]

session-structure¶

A session holds about 40 control trials, 20 to 60 cooling trials and 20 to 80 recovery trials, 80 to 200 trials in all with a mean of 150.

def runs(states):
    out = []

            out[-1][1] += 1
        else:

Result: reproduced. The 45 BEH sessions hold a mean of 143.8 trials (80 to 204), with medians of 39 pre-cooling, 47 cooling and 44 post-cooling trials, all within the criterion. 12 sessions have two cooling blocks, which the paper does not mention. In each of them the second block follows post-cooling trials, and the onset-aligned series used below stops before it.

cooling-time-course¶

MS cooling peaked about 60 s after its onset and lasted about 10 to 12 minutes.

In [18]:
rows = []
for k in TEMP:
    r = beh[k]; t1, T1 = r["temp_1hz_t"], r["temp_1hz"]
    tr = TR[k]
    base = float(np.nanmedian(tr.temperature[tr.state == "Pre-Cooling"]))
    t_first_cool = float(tr.start[tr.state == "Cooling on"].iloc[0])
    after = t1 >= float(tr.start.iloc[0])
    cand = np.flatnonzero(after & (T1 < base - 1) & (t1 > t_first_cool - 600))
    if not len(cand):
        continue
    i0 = cand[0]
    win = (t1 >= t1[i0]) & (t1 <= t1[i0] + 300)
    imin = np.flatnonzero(win)[np.argmin(T1[win])]
    below = np.flatnonzero((t1 > t1[i0]) & (T1 < 32))
    dur32 = np.nan
    if len(below):
        j = below[0]
        back = np.flatnonzero((t1 > t1[j]) & (T1 >= 32))
        dur32 = (t1[back[0]] - t1[j]) / 60 if len(back) else np.nan
    rec = np.flatnonzero((t1 > t1[imin]) & (T1 >= base - 1))
    dur_base = (t1[rec[0]] - t1[i0]) / 60 if len(rec) else np.nan

Result: partially reproduced. The cooling lasted a median 12.16 minutes from onset until the temperature was again within 1 C of baseline (reading b, within 9 to 13.2 minutes; 8.77 minutes below 32 C under reading a). The minimum came a median 121 s after the onset (IQR 89 to 138 s), twice the 60 s of the Methods, and the onset threshold (0.5, 1 or 2 C) does not change this (119 to 122 s). The temperature falls fast and then stays near its minimum: 90% of each session's drop is reached a median 53 s after onset (IQR 44 to 63 s), and the onset-aligned mean trace has its minimum at 121 s and is within 0.5 C of it from 70 to 152 s. Leaving out the five sessions with an artefact baseline above 38 C or an early onset gives 121.5 s to the minimum and 12.22 minutes.

fig2g-theta-freq-temperature¶

Theta frequency decreased linearly with MS temperature (R = 0.81, P = 5.4e-48).

In [19]:
AL = {k: C.aligned_series(TR[k], columns=("error", "temperature", "speed", "theta_freq", "theta_power", "theta_freq_10", "theta_power_10")) for k in BEH}

def stack(keys, col, mask_ms10_temp=False):
    rows = []
    for k in keys:
        x = AL[k][col].copy()
        if mask_ms10_temp and col == "temperature" and k.startswith("MS10"):
            x[:] = np.nan
        rows.append(x)
    return np.vstack(rows)

def mean_series(keys, col, mask=False):
    return np.nanmean(stack(keys, col, mask), axis=0)

pos = np.arange(1, C.ALIGN_LENGTH + 1)
readings = {"(a) TEMP sessions": TEMP, "(b) BEH with MS10 curves": BEH}
res_2g = {}
for name, ks in readings.items():
    r, p, n = C.pearson(mean_series(ks, "temperature"), mean_series(ks, "theta_freq"))
    res_2g[name] = (r, p, n)
    print(f"{name}: R = {r:.3f}, P = {p:.2g}, positions = {n}, sessions = {len(ks)}")
r, p, n = C.pearson(mean_series(TEMP, "temperature"), mean_series(BEH, "theta_freq"))
print(f"variant, temperature over TEMP and theta over BEH (as the code with MS10 temperature missing): R = {r:.3f}, P = {p:.2g}, n = {n}")
r, p, n = C.pearson(mean_series(TEMP, "temperature"), mean_series(TEMP, "theta_freq_10"))
print(f"variant, trial theta over frames above 10 cm/s, TEMP: R = {r:.3f}, P = {p:.2g}")
pooled = pd.concat([TR[k] for k in TEMP])
r, p, n = C.pearson(pooled.temperature, pooled.theta_freq)
sl = np.polyfit(pooled.temperature[pooled.theta_freq.notna()], pooled.theta_freq.dropna(), 1)[0]
print(f"variant, single trials pooled over TEMP: R = {r:.3f}, P = {p:.2g}, trials = {n}, slope {sl:.3f} Hz/C")
print("Expected R 0.81 +- 0.081 with P < 1e-10; within under:", [k for k, v in res_2g.items() if within(v[0], 0.81, 0.081) and v[1] < 1e-10])

Result: reproduced. With the code's onset-aligned series, theta frequency correlates with MS temperature at R = 0.789 (P = 2.8e-43, 198 positions) over the 37 sessions with a recorded temperature, and at R = 0.758 with the MS10 temperature curves included, both within 0.81 +- 0.081. Over single trials pooled the correlation is R = 0.672, with a slope of 0.065 Hz per C.

fig6d-errors-increase¶

MS cooling increased choice errors about 3-fold, within each rat (P < 0.05 for all animals) and across all animals (P = 1e-6).

In [24]:
def rates_table(off_as=None, keys=BEH):
    return pd.DataFrame({k: C.error_rates(TR[k], off_as) for k in keys}).T

er = rates_table()
print(er[["pre", "cooling", "post"]].groupby(lambda k: subj(k)).mean().round(2).to_string())
print("\nMean error rate (%) over", len(er), "sessions: pre", round(er.pre.mean(), 2), ", cooling", round(er.cooling.mean(), 2), ", post", round(er.post.mean(), 2))
ratio_a = er.cooling.mean() / er.pre.mean()
ratio_b = er.cooling.mean() / ((er.pre + er.post) / 2).mean()
ok = er.pre > 0
ratio_c = (er.cooling[ok] / er.pre[ok]).median()
print(f"ratio (a) {ratio_a:.2f}; (b) {ratio_b:.2f}; (c) {ratio_c:.2f} over {int(ok.sum())} sessions with pre > 0 (expected 3.0 +- 0.3)")
p_all, n_all = wsr(er.cooling, er.pre)
print(f"cooling against pre over sessions: higher in {(er.cooling > er.pre).sum()} of {n_all}, signed-rank P = {p_all:.2g}")
rat = {}
for a in sorted({subj(k) for k in BEH}):
    e = er.loc[[k for k in BEH if subj(k) == a]]
    p, n = wsr(e.cooling, e.pre)
    rat[a] = (p, n)
    print(f"  {a}: {n} sessions, pre {e.pre.mean():.1f}%, cooling {e.cooling.mean():.1f}%, ratio {e.cooling.mean() / e.pre.mean():.2f}, higher in {(e.cooling > e.pre).sum()}, P = {p:.3g}")
print("Rats with at least 6 sessions and P < 0.05:", [a for a, (p, n) in rat.items() if n >= 6 and p < 0.05], "of", [a for a, (p, n) in rat.items() if n >= 6])
for off in ["cooling", "post"]:
    e2 = rates_table(off)
    print(f"variant, 'Cooling off' trials counted as {off}: pre {e2.pre.mean():.2f}, cooling {e2.cooling.mean():.2f}, post {e2.post.mean():.2f}, ratio (a) {e2.cooling.mean() / e2.pre.mean():.2f}, P = {wsr(e2.cooling, e2.pre)[0]:.2g}")
e3 = rates_table(keys=TEMP)
print(f"variant, TEMP sessions only: ratio (a) {e3.cooling.mean() / e3.pre.mean():.2f}, P = {wsr(e3.cooling, e3.pre)[0]:.2g}")
e4 = pd.DataFrame({k: C.error_rates(beh[k]["trials"]) for k in BEH + sorted(C.CODE_CONTROLS) + ["MS10-170307-154746"]}).T
print(f"variant, with the two controls and MS10-170307: ratio (a) {e4.cooling.mean() / e4.pre.mean():.2f}, P = {wsr(e4.cooling, e4.pre)[0]:.2g}")
print("Controls alone:", e4.loc[sorted(C.CODE_CONTROLS), ["pre", "cooling", "post"]].round(1).to_dict("index"))

Mean running speed was 87.3 +- 8.0 cm/s in control trials and 86.2 +- 9.9 cm/s during MS cooling.

Result: not reproduced. Over the 15 sessions of the code's Figure 5 list, neither reading gives both values within the paper's spreads. Over all frames the mean speed is 78.9 cm/s in control trials and 74.9 cm/s during cooling, both outside. Over frames above 10 cm/s control is 79.6 cm/s, within 87.3 +- 8.0, and cooling 76.0 cm/s, just below 86.2 +- 9.9. Speed is lower during cooling than in control (P = 0.035 to 0.041), where the paper's values are close to each other.

suppl2-place-cell-rates-decrease¶

Within-field and peak firing rates of place cells decreased moderately during MS cooling (11% and 12%; P < 1e-9 and P < 1e-11).

In [34]:

    pc = 100 * (1 - Fr[f"{m}_cooling"] / Fr[f"{m}_pre"])
    a, b, c = pc.median(), 100 * (1 - Fr[f"{m}_cooling"].mean() / Fr[f"{m}_pre"].mean()), pc.mean()
    p, n = wsr(Fr[f"{m}_cooling"], Fr[f"{m}_pre"])
    res_r[m] = (a, b, c, p)
    print(f"{m}: pre mean {Fr[m + '_pre'].mean():.2f} Hz, cooling {Fr[m + '_cooling'].mean():.2f} Hz; decrease (a) median {a:.1f}%, (b) ratio of means {b:.1f}%, "
          f"(c) mean {c:.1f}%; signed-rank P = {p:.2g} (n = {n}); lower in {(Fr[m + '_cooling'] < Fr[m + '_pre']).sum()}")
    pp, nn = wsr(Fr[f"{m}_post"], Fr[f"{m}_cooling"])
    print(f"   post against cooling: post mean {Fr[m + '_post'].mean():.2f} Hz, P = {pp:.2g}")
    print("   by subject, reading (b):", {a_: round(100 * (1 - g[f'{m}_cooling'].mean() / g[f'{m}_pre'].mean()), 1) for a_, g in Fr.groupby("subject")})

for m in ["ttp", "amp"]:
    p, n = wsr(wv[f"{m}_cooling"], wv[f"{m}_pre"])
    d = wv[f"{m}_cooling"] - wv[f"{m}_pre"]
    print(f"{m}: pre median {wv[m + '_pre'].median():.3f}, cooling median {wv[m + '_cooling'].median():.3f}; median change {d.median():.4f} "
          f"({100 * (d / wv[m + '_pre']).median():.1f}%), mean change {d.mean():.4f}; higher in {(d > 0).sum()}, lower in {(d < 0).sum()}, equal in {(d == 0).sum()}; "
          f"signed-rank P = {p:.2g} (n = {n})")
print("Spikes averaged per unit, median (IQR): pre", wv.nwf_pre.median(), wv.nwf_pre.quantile([.25, .75]).tolist(),
      "; cooling", wv.nwf_cooling.median(), wv.nwf_cooling.quantile([.25, .75]).tolist(), "; fewer in cooling than pre in", int((wv.nwf_cooling < wv.nwf_pre).sum()), "units")

print(f"units with at least 300 spikes in both windows, so both means use the 300-spike cap (n = {len(cap)}): amplitude median change "
      f"{100 * ((cap.amp_cooling - cap.amp_pre) / cap.amp_pre).median():.1f}%, P = {wsr(cap.amp_cooling, cap.amp_pre)[0]:.2g}; "
      f"ttp higher in {(cap.ttp_cooling > cap.ttp_pre).sum()}, lower in {(cap.ttp_cooling < cap.ttp_pre).sum()}, P = {wsr(cap.ttp_cooling, cap.ttp_pre)[0]:.2g}")
print("Units whose largest channel moved between windows:", int((wv.chan_pre != wv.chan_cooling).sum()))
for t_ in ["pyramidal", "interneuron"]:
    g = wv[wv.cell_type == t_]
    print(f"  {t_} (n = {len(g)}): ttp P = {wsr(g.ttp_cooling, g.ttp_pre)[0]:.2g}, amplitude change {100 * ((g.amp_cooling - g.amp_pre) / g.amp_pre).median():.1f}%, P = {wsr(g.amp_cooling, g.amp_pre)[0]:.2g}")
for mins in [50, 100]:
    g = UC[(UC.nwf_pre >= mins) & (UC.nwf_cooling >= mins)]
    print(f"variant, at least {mins} spikes (n = {len(g)}): ttp P = {wsr(g.ttp_cooling, g.ttp_pre)[0]:.2g}, amplitude P = {wsr(g.amp_cooling, g.amp_pre)[0]:.2g}, "
          f"median amplitude change {100 * ((g.amp_cooling - g.amp_pre) / g.amp_pre).median():.1f}%")

Result: not reproduced. Across 646 units the waveforms differ between the pre window and the coldest cooling window: trough-to-peak by the signed-rank test (P = 4.9e-10, median change 0, since most units do not change by a whole 0.05 ms sample) and amplitude by a median 0.8% (P = 0.00057). Fewer spikes are averaged in the cooling window (median 200 against 247.5), but in the 208 units whose two means both use 300 spikes the changes remain (amplitude 0.7%, P = 0.032; trough-to-peak P = 2.2e-05), so the spike count does not explain them. Both changes are small, and the two windows start 7.1 to 31.8 minutes apart (printed above), so electrode drift cannot be told apart from cooling here; for interneurons alone neither differs (P = 0.066 and 0.2).

fig4b-fp-flfp-decrease¶

MS cooling decreased both the oscillation frequency of place cells (fp) and the LFP theta frequency in their fields (fLFP) by about the same degree, and both recovered (fLFP 8.4, 7.7, 8.5 Hz; fp 10.6, 9.5, 10.4 Hz before, during and after; n = 365).

Result: reproduced. Over 361 place fields (the paper has 365), fLFP is 8.54, 7.77 and 8.60 Hz and fp 10.55, 9.57 and 10.39 Hz before, during and after cooling, all six within the paper's spreads. Both fall during cooling (fp in 311 fields, P = 3.5e-44; fLFP in 352, P = 1.2e-60) by 9.2% and 9.0%, and both recover (P = 4.5e-37 and 6.8e-61). Each rat shows the same pattern, and every session shows the decrease; fp does not recover in MS22-180720-110055 (9.92 Hz after, 10.15 Hz during cooling). Fields with at least 100 or 200 spikes per state give the same means.

fp and fLFP were correlated across place fields before, during and after cooling (R = 0.61, 0.59 and 0.36; P < 1e-6 each).

fig4ac-fp-flfp-difference-preserved¶

During MS cooling fp and fLFP decreased in parallel, so the difference fp - fLFP remained constant.

Result: not reproduced. fp - fLFP falls from 2.009 Hz before cooling to 1.806 Hz during it (median change -0.128 Hz, P = 0.000132), so the difference is not preserved by the paper's default test, and it stays at 1.790 Hz after cooling (P = 0.98 against cooling). The ratio fp/fLFP is preserved (1.237 and 1.232, P = 0.84). The change differs between rats (MS12 -1.03 Hz, MS13 and MS22 near 0).

fig4a-frequency-temperature-slopes¶

fLFP and fp measured within place fields decreased linearly with MS temperature (fLFP R = 0.66, slope 0.071 Hz per C; fp R = 0.38, slope 0.09 Hz per C).

Result: partially reproduced. Over 52474 windows of 20 trials, fLFP rises with temperature at R = 0.678 and 0.0716 Hz per C, and fp at a slope of 0.0859 Hz per C, all three within tolerance; the fp correlation is R = 0.338, just below 0.38 +- 0.038. The windows overlap (stepped by one trial), so the P values over windows overstate the evidence.

fig3e-model-field-size¶

Measured place field size correlated with the size predicted by SPF = v / (fp - fLFP) before (R = 0.55) and during (R = 0.54) cooling, and weakly after (R = 0.11).

In [44]:
exp3e = {"pre": (0.55, 0.055), "cooling": (0.54, 0.054), "post": (0.11, 0.011)}
for st, (v, tol) in exp3e.items():
    dfq = F3[f"fp_{st}"] - F3[f"flfp_{st}"]
    ok = dfq > 0.2
    pred = F3.loc[ok, f"v_{st}"] / dfq[ok]
    r, p, n = C.pearson(F3.loc[ok, f"size_{st}"], pred)
    print(f"{st}: fields {n} (of {len(F3)}), R = {r:.3f}, P = {p:.2g} (expected {v} +- {tol}); within: {within(r, v, tol)}; "
          f"median predicted {pred.median():.1f} cm, measured {F3.loc[ok, f'size_{st}'].median():.1f} cm")
    rs = stats.spearmanr(F3.loc[ok, f"size_{st}"], pred)[0]
    print(f"   variant, Spearman rho = {rs:.3f}; by subject R:", {a: round(C.pearson(F3.loc[ok & (F3.subject == a), f"size_{st}"], pred[F3.loc[ok, 'subject'] == a])[0], 2) for a in sorted(F3.subject.unique())})

Result: not reproduced. The paper's default paired test finds information content lower during cooling than before (median change -0.029 against a median of 1.253 bits/spike, P = 0.014 over 374 place cells) and lower after cooling than before (P = 0.0064); cooling and post do not differ (P = 0.31). With each state's spikes subsampled to the same count (360 cells), pre against cooling still gives P = 0.0073 and pre against post P = 0.0092, so the decrease does not come from the different numbers of spikes in the states.

The phase precession slope decreased slightly but significantly during MS cooling (P < 0.007 and P < 0.0003).

fig4gh-fp-speed¶

fp depended on running speed more strongly than fLFP, and fp during cooling was lower at all velocities.

In [48]:
rng_4gh = np.random.default_rng(4)
bins = list(range(20, 120, 20))
long = []
for _, r_ in F.iterrows():
    for st in ["pre", "cooling", "post"]:
        for b in bins:
            fp_, fl_ = r_[f"fp_{st}_v{b}"], r_[f"flfp_{st}_v{b}"]
            if np.isfinite(fp_) and np.isfinite(fl_):
                long.append({"field": (r_.session, r_.unit, r_.field), "state": st, "speed": b + 10, "fp": fp_, "flfp": fl_})
L = pd.DataFrame(long)
print("Field, state and speed-bin values:", len(L), "from", L.field.nunique(), "fields; per bin:", L.groupby("speed").size().to_dict())
s_fp = stats.linregress(L.speed, L.fp); s_fl = stats.linregress(L.speed, L.flfp)
print(f"fp slope {s_fp.slope:.4f} Hz per cm/s (P = {s_fp.pvalue:.2g}); fLFP slope {s_fl.slope:.4f} (P = {s_fl.pvalue:.2g})")
codes = pd.factorize(L.field)[0]
rows_by = [np.flatnonzero(codes == i) for i in range(codes.max() + 1)]
boot = []
for _ in range(1000):
    pick = rng_4gh.integers(0, len(rows_by), len(rows_by))
    ii = np.concatenate([rows_by[i] for i in pick])
    x = L.speed.values[ii]
    boot.append(np.polyfit(x, L.fp.values[ii], 1)[0] - np.polyfit(x, L.flfp.values[ii], 1)[0])
lo, hi = np.percentile(boot, [2.5, 97.5])
print(f"difference of slopes (fp minus fLFP) {s_fp.slope - s_fl.slope:.4f}, 95% bootstrap interval over fields {lo:.4f} to {hi:.4f}")
print("\nMedian fp by speed bin, fields measured in both pre and cooling:")
part2 = []
for b in bins:
    pr = L[(L.state == "pre") & (L.speed == b + 10)].set_index("field").fp
    co = L[(L.state == "cooling") & (L.speed == b + 10)].set_index("field").fp
    both = pr.index.intersection(co.index)
    if len(both) >= 10:
        part2.append(co[both].median() < pr[both].median())
        print(f"  {b}-{b + 20} cm/s: n = {len(both)}, pre {pr[both].median():.2f}, cooling {co[both].median():.2f} Hz, P = {wsr(co[both], pr[both])[0]:.2g}")
    else:
        print(f"  {b}-{b + 20} cm/s: n = {len(both)} (fewer than 10)")
print("fp lower during cooling in every bin with at least 10 fields:", all(part2), f"({sum(part2)} of {len(part2)})")
print("Mean fp and fLFP by speed bin (all states):", L.groupby("speed")[["fp", "flfp"]].mean().round(2).to_dict("index"))

fig5d-ccg-period¶

The theta-repeated cross-correlograms of place cell pairs had a period of about 85 ms before cooling, which lengthened during MS cooling (P = 0.002), while the period of the phase cross-correlograms was unaffected (P = 0.32).

# variant: period of the summed correlogram of all pairs, by spectral peak and by the fit
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
for k in FIG5:
    cs = units[k]["ccg_sum"]
    ctl = cs["pre"]["time"] + cs["post"]["time"]
    sp_ = []
    for c in [ctl, cs["cooling"]["time"]]:
        res = c - gaussian_filter1d(c, 40, mode="nearest")
        sel = np.abs(C.TIME_LAGS) <= 300
        z = res[sel] * np.hanning(sel.sum()); spec = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(z, 1 << 16)); fr = np.fft.rfftfreq(1 << 16, 0.001)
        band = (fr >= 5) & (fr <= 14); sp_.append(1000 / fr[band][np.argmax(spec[band])])
    print(f"variant, summed correlogram spectral period {k}: control {sp_[0]:.1f}, cooling {sp_[1]:.1f} ms")

Result: partially reproduced. Under the criterion's estimator the period of the pair cross-correlograms lengthens during cooling, from a median 109.2 to 114.0 ms (longer in 8 of 9 sessions, P = 0.0195), and the phase period does not change (1.740 and 1.760 pi rad, P = 0.59), but the control period is 109.2 ms, not 85 +- 8.5 ms. That estimator takes the largest neighbouring peak within 60 to 200 ms, and in 47.7% of pre pairs this peak is more than 1.25 times as far as the nearest one, so it often picks the second neighbour. Taking the nearest neighbouring peak (a variant) gives a control period of 91.0 ms, within tolerance, which lengthens to 95.5 ms during cooling (7 of 9 sessions, P = 0.031); pairs with |Ltr| below 10 cm give 91.0 ms. Under that variant the phase period does not change either (1.285 pi rad in both, P = 0.367). The nearest-peak estimator is biased the other way: 211 of 3499 pre pairs have a period of 60 to 70 ms, below any plausible theta period, at the floor of the 60 ms search window, so its 91.0 ms is not a clean test of 85 ms either. Both control periods are shorter than the LFP theta period (115.7 ms), as the paper says of its 85 ms.

fig5cg-compression¶

Distance-time compression of place cell pairs (0.54 cm/ms before cooling) decreased during MS cooling (P = 0.02), while distance-phase compression was unchanged (P = 0.92).

def slope_xy(x, y):
    ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    if ok.sum() < 5:
        return np.nan
    return float(np.polyfit(x[ok], y[ok], 1)[0])

Result: not reproduced. The distance-time compression over pooled pre pairs is 0.273 cm/ms, half of 0.54, and the per-session compression is lower during cooling in 8 of 9 sessions without reaching significance (0.298 against 0.191 cm/ms, P = 0.0547). The phase compression does not change (P = 0.426). Time lag and distance correlate weakly in these pairs (R = 0.195), so the slope depends on the fit: the inverse regression over pooled pre pairs gives 7.175 cm/ms. In 10.5% of pre pairs the lag changes when the window is narrowed to half the theta period, and that window gives 0.156 cm/ms, so the compression magnitude depends on how the lag is picked and cannot be judged from this method. The direction of the change also depends on the fit: the inverse slope is higher during cooling (9.085 against 10.420 cm/ms, lower in 1 of 9 sessions).

Result: not reproduced. Phase lags are slightly larger during cooling than before (median 1.367 against 1.304 rad, mean difference 0.051 rad, P = 0.0015) and after (P = 0.0043), and before and after do not differ (P = 0.51). The change is small, but by the paper's test the phase lags are not preserved. The +-pi window spans about 1.15 periods of the phase correlogram, so it can hold two candidate peaks. With the lag picked within +-pi/2 (a variant), 43.3% of pre pairs get another lag or none (293 have no peak in the window); cooling is still above pre (mean difference 0.025 rad, P = 0.0196) but not above post (P = 0.162), and pre and post do not differ (P = 0.178). Part of the increase may come from how the lag is picked; the increase over pre remains.

Result: not reproduced. Over 9037 pre and 10152 cooling theta cycles, the fraction of place cells active per cycle is higher during cooling (mean 0.2405 against 0.226, rank-sum P = 1.5e-22). Per session the cooling mean is lower than pre in 5 of 9 sessions (P = 0.734), and cooling does not differ from post (P = 0.074), while pre and post differ (P = 0.004). The pooled test mixes sessions whose means range from 0.159 to 0.315 and that contribute different numbers of cycles in each state, so it reflects the make-up of the pool as much as an effect. Cycles are longer during cooling (131.1 ms against 117.8 and 117.2 ms).

print("variant, session means, signed-rank:", {f"{a} vs {b}": round(wsr(sesk[a], sesk[b])[0], 3) for a, b in [("pre", "cooling"), ("cooling", "post"), ("pre", "post")]})
norm = CY.groupby("session").spikes.transform("mean")
print("variant, spikes per cycle over each session's mean, by state:", (CY.spikes / norm).groupby(CY.state).mean().round(3).to_dict())

Result: not reproduced. Spikes per theta cycle do not differ between pre and cooling (45.68 and 44.98, P = 0.0758) but are higher after cooling (51.68) than during it or before it (both P below 1e-50), so not all comparisons are null. Per session, cooling differs from neither pre (P = 0.57) nor post (P = 0.129), and post differs from pre (P = 0.02). Session means range from 17.66 to 91.37 spikes, so the pooled tests depend on how many cycles each session contributes.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. 45 of the paper's 53 sessions have cooling states here (six are not deposited, one lacks states, one lacks trials); temperature analyses use the 37 with a recorded temperature. Cell types are not in the files and were made here from waveform width and rate. Place fields use the automatic criteria the Methods give for Figure 5, for all figures, where the paper defined fields by hand for Figures 3 and 4. Pair lags are the peak of each pair's correlogram and compression a regression, where the paper fits a surface to the density of all pairs. The CCG period is measured per pair, with an estimator that often picks the second neighbouring peak (the nearest-peak variant is shown). Units come from 11 sessions in 4 rats (the paper's Figure 5 has 18 sessions in 5 rats); MS10 has no curated units. Two unit sessions were left out because spikes carry no spatial information there.

What was found about the dandiset. The temperature of the nine MS10 sessions and of the two control sessions of 2018-07-19 is not a recording (the paper's code lists no temperature channel for them); it runs from 17 to 37 C (exactly in nine of ten), or is constant. The two controls also carry cooling labels although the code describes them as sessions without cooling, and their theta does not slow as in cooled sessions. Six of the paper's sessions are missing, one session has no cooling states and one no trials. No file holds cell types, place fields or electrode locations, and the units of seven sessions are all 'unsorted'. The trial state 'Cooling off' is not described. In two sessions spikes carry no spatial information. The first published version has no trials table.
